comparator.sourceNotes: Current programme-specific and general Faculty of Arts OER together govern the English IBC specialisation within BA Communication and Information Studies (56826), fulltime, 180 EC. Cohort starting 2026: 60 EC B1 +30 EC B2 core +30 EC two fixed Faculty of Arts minors +10 EC B3 PPD +5 EC Cross-cultural Language Use English +5 EC Academic and Professional Language Skills English +30 EC broadening bachelor electives +10 EC thesis. Free space cannot contain own-programme/other-specialisation courses; foreign study requires approval six working weeks before departure. Language courses must stay in one language. Spanish is a separate optional route, not an added English requirement. Zero-EC B1/B2 mentorship/portfolio and compulsory RADAr participation are not extra credits; workshops recommended. Attendance applies to mentorship and seminars; over35%absence in a period excludes participation subject to examiner exception. Practical assignments may condition exams. BSA45EC. Thesis starts only in semester2ofB3 under programme Article10 and current course foreknowledge, despite generic course text mentioning two intake dates; pre-register theme and Osiris. Online cross-cultural and English language-use courses presume basic statistics/SPSS. Course204 has misplaced Spanish foreknowledge text; not applied to English route. Prospective pages indicate2027–30 and differ in B3: do not replace current required English language skills with future Misinformation/Persuasion or Advanced Intercultural Communication. alternatives.concept: Leadership communication, marketing, diversity and organisational behaviour combine with rhetoric, persuasion and market research. International business and digital strategy provide organisational context; qualitative, statistical and data courses support empirical inquiry. Film history, literary stylistics and documentary work add cultural analysis. This is a related business-communication route with limited language-specific and cross-cultural research coverage; it does not reproduce Radboud’s advanced English sequence or thesis.

alternatives.concept: Rhetoric, applied persuasion, climate communication and documentary analysis combine with public health, human rights, environmental justice, civil society and youth-resilience work. alternativeSelection.assessment: Two supported, distinct routes respond to business/organisational and public/social communication interests. The proposed digital route lacks defining communication/language research beyond general computing/media; Spanish and a dedicated advanced English/cross-cultural sequence are unavailable. Three is a maximum, not a target.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop personal and professional reflection and academic skills, with different placement and scope: UCR requires this in year one.
Rhetorical history, argument and speaking/writing skills contribute to communication foundations; they cover part of the broader CIS introduction.
Film form, cinema history and cultural analysis provide a partial media perspective, with only brief wider digital-media coverage.
Research design, experiments, surveys and statistics contribute to academic inquiry; not all language-specific academic skills.
Leadership communication models, emotional intelligence, culture and practice contribute to organisational communication, with a narrower leadership focus.
Multivariate statistics and behavioural analysis provide related analytical tools; the target also requires designing and reporting communication experiments.
General data cleaning and visualisation provide transferable data skills; the target uses a communication context.
Persuasion models, framing, ethics and real communication challenges provide substantive related coverage.
Consumer psychology, brands and strategic marketing plans contribute to marketing communication.
Diversity and inclusive organisational leadership offer related work across differences, rather than the complete intercultural communication research course.

audience.programmeDescription: International Business Communication is the English-taught specialisation of Radboud’s Communication and Information Studies degree. It studies language and communication in multilingual organisations, combining corporate, intercultural and marketing communication with qualitative and quantitative research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two UCR routes offer related study in business communication or public/social communication. Rhetoric, leadership, marketing, applied persuasion and research methods provide substantial connections. Film and media history, literary stylistics and subject courses broaden the context. They do not replace dedicated intercultural language research, advanced professional English, the complete digital communication sequence or the required IBC thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC framework includes 90 EC of required first/second-year courses, two 15 EC Faculty of Arts minors, 10 EC personal and professional development, two 5 EC English-language components, 30 EC broadening bachelor electives and a 10 EC thesis. Earlier mentoring and the compulsory academic-language diagnostic test add no credits. Prospective 2027–2030 tables describe later curricula and are not substituted here. Rhetoric in Action at UCR involves local schoolchildren and principally Dutch interaction; students should check project language arrangements.
